references.text: Basic principle regarding sins committed unintentionally (בִּשְׁגָגָה), which also applies to the ruler in verse 22
Expands on the laws concerning sins committed unintentionally and the guilt offering required
Parallel structure for common people who sin unintentionally, corresponding to the situation of the ruler
Describes נָשִׂיא (ruler/leader) and their role and responsibility in Israel
The ruler (נָשִׂיא) must offer a bull as a sin offering for himself and the people
Concerns guilt (וְאָשֵׁם) for one who sins against the Lord's command without knowing it
The high priest must bear with the ignorant and those who err, and make atonement for his own sins
Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point is guilty of breaking all
